analysis.evidence: God promises Abram that he will bless מְבָרְכֶיךָ, “those who bless you.” The parallel promise אָאֹר, “I will curse,” confirms that God is the one who acts in response to how people treat Abram.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ means “and.” The verb is a Piel first-person common singular cohortative, marked by the first-person prefix אֲ־ and the ending ־ָה. It expresses the speaker’s resolve.
analysis.sense: to confer divine blessing on a person

analysis.evidence: In וַאֲבָרֲכָה מְבָרְכֶיךָ, God promises to bless the people who bless Abram. The parallel וּמְקַלֶּלְךָ אָאֹר contrasts them with the person who curses him.
analysis.morphology: The Piel active participle is masculine plural in the construct state and functions as a noun meaning “those who bless.” The second-person masculine singular suffix ךָ supplies its object, Abram.
analysis.sense: to speak a blessing upon another person

analysis.evidence: The verse pairs מְבָרְכֶיךָ, “those who bless you,” with וּמְקַלֶּלְךָ, “and the one who curses you.” God promises to bless the former and says of the latter, אָאֹר, “I will curse.”
analysis.gloss: and the one who curses you
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ precedes a Piel active participle in the masculine singular construct. The participle functions as a noun, and its second-person masculine singular suffix identifies Abram as the one being cursed.

draft.change: Broaden the proposed Qal definition to include a curse pronounced on a thing, and cite the feminine participle applied to the ground.
draft.definition: To pronounce a curse on someone or something. The passive participle describes whoever or whatever is under the curse.
draft.evidence: In Gen.3.17 Yahweh addresses Adam, but the subject of אֲרוּרָה is הָאֲדָמָה, the ground. In Gen.3.14 the corresponding masculine form אָרוּר describes the serpent.

analysis.evidence: The speaker promises Abram, “I will bless those who bless you.” In the matching clause, וּמְקַלֶּלְךָ supplies the object of אָאֹר, “the one who curses you I will curse.”
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, first person common singular. The initial אָ marks the first person. The verb has no attached pronoun.
analysis.sense: To pronounce a curse on someone or something.

analysis.evidence: The plural verb agrees with its following subject, כֹּל מִשְׁפְּחֹת הָאֲדָמָה, “all the families of the earth.” בְךָ, “in you,” refers to Abram, whom God is addressing.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ joins a Niphal perfect, third person common plural, to the preceding promise. In this sequence the verb has future force.

analysis.evidence: כֹּל governs the definite plural phrase מִשְׁפְּחֹת הָאֲדָמָה, “the families of the earth.” The promise of blessing extends to all of those families.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: מִשְׁפְּחֹת takes הָאֲדָמָה as its complement. The full phrase כֹּל מִשְׁפְּחֹת הָאֲדָמָה means “all the families of the earth” and identifies those included in the blessing.
analysis.morphology: Feminine plural common noun in the construct state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The promise extends to כֹּל מִשְׁפְּחֹת הָאֲדָמָה, “all the families of the earth.” The reference to all families gives הָאֲדָמָה its worldwide scope.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a feminine singular common noun in the absolute state. The noun completes the construct phrase כֹּל מִשְׁפְּחֹת הָאֲדָמָה.
analysis.sense: the earth, as where all peoples live
